history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V25 workload, representation, width, job count, checksum, execution mode, scored operation, attribution counter, timing boundary, measured-boundary occupancy rule, logical-versus-binary revision contract, and publication ruling. It adds only strict untimed native allocation replay attachment and strictly serial batch-row collection under one Home compilation. Historical artifacts remain byte-identical.
change: Adds an optional native attribution replay after each measured invocation and a serial batch-row interface. The replay must contain exactly one invocation-phase record with matching identity, checksum, required tier boundary, and positive Context backing allocation counters. Replays remain outside elapsed_ns. Batch rows share one Home compilation but launch benchmark children strictly serially and retain one independently validated artifact per row.

exact_parent_integration.publication_boundary: V26 preserves V25 measured-boundary CPU, hardware, thermal, order balancing, checksum, cleanliness, and shared-overlay gates. Native allocation replays are untimed, identity-bound, and exact; serial batches cannot overlap benchmark children or merge row artifacts.

instrumentation_overhead_integration.evidence_ruling: Unchanged V25 parser and historical disabled-path evidence; V26 adds untimed allocation replay and serial batch collection only.

context_lifecycle_integration.publication_boundary: Unchanged V25 lifecycle scenarios, telemetry, checksums, reconciliation, plateau, measured-boundary occupancy, and binary provenance.

no_jit_integration.publication_boundary: Unchanged V25 required-bytecode modes, logical work, checksums, attribution, quickening, measured-boundary occupancy, and binary provenance.

string_indexing_integration.publication_boundary: Unchanged V25 string representations, widths, jobs, checksums, attribution, timing, and non-throughput boundary. V26 permits the already-frozen attribution_no_jit replay to populate exact allocation metrics outside elapsed_ns and collects rows strictly serially.
